name: STM32F303K8T6
title: STM32F303x6/x8: 72 MHz Arm Cortex-M4 microcontrollers with FPU, 32 KB or 64 KB flash, 2 ADCs, 3 DACs, 3 comparators and an op-amp, 2.0 V to 3.6 V
summary: A family of 32-bit Arm Cortex-M4 microcontrollers with a single-precision floating-point unit and DSP instructions, running to 72 MHz from a 2.0 V to 3.6 V supply. Each part has 32 KB or 64 KB of flash, 12 KB of parity-checked SRAM plus 4 KB of core-coupled SRAM, two 5 MSPS 12-bit ADCs, three 12-bit DAC channels, up to three fast rail-to-rail comparators, one programmable-gain op-amp, a 7-channel DMA, up to 11 timers, a calendar RTC with VBAT backup, CAN, I2C, SPI and up to three USARTs, in LQFP32, LQFP48 and LQFP64. The STM32F303K8T6 is the LQFP32 part with 64 KB of flash, rated -40 °C to 85 °C ambient.
key_figures: Core
Arm Cortex-M4 with FPU, 72 MHz max, 90 DMIPS running from CCM SRAM
Flash / SRAM
32 KB (x6) or 64 KB (x8) flash; 12 KB SRAM + 4 KB CCM SRAM, both with parity
Supply
VDD 2.0 V to 3.6 V; VDDA 2.0 V to 3.6 V (2.4 V min for DAC and op-amp); VBAT 1.65 V to 3.6 V
Run current
71.4 mA typ at 72 MHz from flash, all peripherals on, HSE bypass (VDD = 3.6 V); 25.2 mA typ at 72 MHz, peripherals off (VDD = 3.3 V)
Stop / Standby
Stop 6.96 µA typ from VDD (regulator low-power, VDD = 3.3 V); Standby 0.93 µA typ (LSI and IWDG off, VDD = 3.3 V)
ADC
two 12-bit 5 MSPS ADCs, up to 21 channels (9 on the LQFP32), single-ended or differential
Analog
3 DAC channels (one buffered), up to 3 comparators, 1 op-amp with PGA gain 2/4/8/16
Clocks
HSI 8 MHz, HSE 4 MHz to 32 MHz, LSI 40 kHz, LSE 32.768 kHz, PLL to 72 MHz
I/O
up to 51 GPIOs; LQFP32: 25 (10 TC/TTa, 15 FT/FTf)
Interfaces
CAN 2.0B, I2C (1 MHz FM+), SPI (18 Mbit/s), up to 3 USARTs (9 Mbit/s), SWD/JTAG
Temperature
-40 °C to 85 °C (suffix 6) or -40 °C to 105 °C (suffix 7) ambient; junction -40 °C to 125 °C
Packages
LQFP32 7 × 7 mm, LQFP48 7 × 7 mm, LQFP64 10 × 10 mm

notes: (1) Counts the PWM outputs on the complementary channels as well.

Common to all six: one 16-bit advanced-control timer, four 16-bit and one 32-bit general-purpose timers, two 16-bit basic timers, SysTick, two watchdogs (independent, window), one SPI, one I2C, one CAN, 7 DMA channels, three 12-bit DAC channels, one op-amp, 72 MHz CPU, 2.0 V to 3.6 V.
Ambient range -40 °C to 85 °C or -40 °C to 105 °C by temperature code; junction -40 °C to 125 °C.

STM32F303x6 is the K6, C6 and R6; STM32F303x8 the K8, C8 and R8. The full order code (STM32F303K8T6) adds the package letter T (LQFP) and the temperature code 6 (-40 °C to 85 °C) or 7 (-40 °C to 105 °C).

circuits.title: Typical application with an 8 MHz crystal
circuits.description: An 8 MHz crystal or ceramic resonator runs the high-speed oscillator. One end goes straight to OSC_IN, the other reaches OSC_OUT through REXT, and each end has a load capacitor to ground. The 200 kΩ feedback resistor RF is inside the chip. CL1 and CL2 are usually equal high-quality ceramics of about 5 pF to 25 pF, sized so that their series value plus about 10 pF of pin and board capacitance matches the crystal's load; REXT is chosen for the crystal. A resonator with built-in capacitors replaces Y1, C1 and C2. All of it sits close to the pins.

circuits.title: Typical application with a 32.768 kHz crystal
circuits.description: A 32.768 kHz crystal or resonator across OSC32_IN and OSC32_OUT runs the low-speed oscillator for the RTC, with a load capacitor from each end to ground, placed close to the pins. No resistor goes between OSC32_IN and OSC32_OUT: one is not needed and must not be fitted. A resonator with built-in capacitors replaces Y1, C1 and C2.
notes: OSC32_IN and OSC32_OUT are PC14 and PC15, on the LQFP48 and LQFP64 only.
Misprint: the 32.768 kHz figure is labelled with the 8 MHz parts (OSC_IN, OSC_OUT, REXT); it should show OSC32_IN and OSC32_OUT with no resistor between them.

circuits.title: Recommended NRST pin protection
circuits.description: A 0.1 µF capacitor from NRST to ground, as close to the chip as possible, keeps stray pulses from resetting it, and a push button to ground gives a manual reset. Inside, NRST has a pull-up RPU (40 kΩ typ) to VDD, a Schmitt input and a pulse filter. Whatever drives NRST must pull it below VIL(NRST) max or the reset is not seen.
notes: NRST is LQFP32 pin 4.

circuits.description: A source VAIN drives an analog input AINx through its own resistance RAIN; Cparasitic, the board capacitance plus about 7 pF of pad, loads the pin. Inside, the pin has 0.6 V clamp diodes to VDD and ground, up to ±1 µA of leakage, and samples through RADC onto CADC. RAIN stays under the maximum for the sampling time and resolution; a large Cparasitic hurts accuracy, which a lower fADC recovers.

operation.text: Arm Cortex-M4 32-bit core with a single-precision FPU and the DSP instruction set; single-cycle multiply and hardware divide. It reaches 90 Dhrystone MIPS at 72 MHz when code runs from the CCM SRAM.

Up to 64 KB of flash holds code and data. Flash wait states follow the CPU clock: none up to 24 MHz, one from 24 MHz to 48 MHz, two above. SRAM is 12 KB on the data bus plus 4 KB of core-coupled memory (CCM) on both the instruction and data buses for time-critical routines; both carry hardware parity and run at CPU speed with no wait states.

The BOOT0 pin and the BOOT1 option bit, sampled at start-up, choose one of three boot sources: user flash, system memory or the embedded SRAM. System memory holds a boot loader that reprograms the flash over USART1 (PA9/PA10), USART2 (PA2/PA3) or I2C1 (PB6/PB7).
A CRC calculator with a configurable generator polynomial and size, usable to check flash contents at run time against a signature stored at link time (an EN/IEC 60335-1 measure).

VDD (2.0 V to 3.6 V) feeds the I/Os and the internal regulator. VDDA (2.0 V to 3.6 V) feeds the ADCs, DACs, comparators, op-amp, reset blocks, RC oscillators and PLL; ADC and comparators work from 2 V, DAC and op-amp need 2.4 V. VDDA must be at or above VDD at all times and must come up first. The regulator makes the 1.65 V to 1.95 V VDD18 core domain (core, SRAM, flash). VBAT (1.65 V to 3.6 V) keeps the RTC, the 32 kHz oscillator and the backup registers running through a power switch when VDD is absent.

Power-on and power-down reset circuits are always on and hold the part in reset below the VPOR/PDR threshold, so no external reset circuit is needed; operation is guaranteed above 2 V. The POR watches VDD only. The PDR watches VDD and VDDA; its VDDA monitor can be turned off by an option bit to save current when the design guarantees VDDA ≥ VDD. A software-enabled programmable voltage detector (PVD) compares VDD with a selectable VPVD threshold and can raise an interrupt as VDD falls below or rises above it.

The internal regulator runs in main mode in Run, low-power mode in Stop, and is powered down in Standby, where its output goes high-impedance and the core domain draws nothing. It is on after every reset.
Only the CPU stops; peripherals keep running and any interrupt or event wakes it.

Lowest power with SRAM and register contents kept: all 1.8 V-domain clocks stop and the PLL, HSI and HSE are off; the regulator stays in normal or low-power mode. Any EXTI line wakes the part: one of the 16 external lines, the PVD, the RTC alarm, a comparator, I2C or a USART.

The regulator is off and the whole 1.8 V domain loses power, as do the PLL, HSI and HSE; SRAM and registers are lost except the backup domain and standby circuitry. Exit is by NRST, an IWDG reset, a rising edge on a WKUP pin or an RTC alarm. The RTC, the IWDG and their clocks keep running in Stop and Standby.

Peripherals signal one another directly in hardware (timer to ADC/DAC triggers, comparator to timer break and capture, ADC watchdog to TIM1, DAC to comparator input and so on), with fixed latency and no CPU involvement.

The 8 MHz internal RC (HSI) is the CPU clock after reset. A 4 MHz to 32 MHz external clock or crystal (HSE) can be selected and is watched by the clock security system: on failure the system falls back to the HSI and can raise an interrupt. Prescalers set the AHB, APB2 (high-speed) and APB1 (low-speed) clocks: AHB and APB2 to 72 MHz, APB1 to 36 MHz. TIM1 runs to 144 MHz. The PLL takes HSI/2 or HSE (divided by 1 to 16) and multiplies by 2 to 16. Other sources: the 40 kHz LSI for the IWDG and RTC, the 32.768 kHz LSE for the RTC, and HSE/32 for the RTC. An MCO pin can output a selected clock through a divider of 1 to 128.

Each GPIO can be a push-pull or open-drain output, an input (floating, pulled up or pulled down), or an alternate function of a peripheral. All are high-current capable except those used as analog inputs. The alternate-function configuration can be locked against stray writes. I/O can toggle at up to 36 MHz.

Seven DMA channels, each tied to hardware requests and also software-triggerable, that move data from memory or a peripheral to memory or a peripheral with circular buffers and independent source and destination sizes. SPI, I2C, USART, the general-purpose timers, DAC and ADC can use it.

The NVIC handles up to 60 maskable interrupt channels with 16 priority levels, with tail chaining and automatic state saving. The EXTI has 27 edge-detecting lines, each set for rising, falling or both edges and maskable on its own; it catches pulses narrower than one internal clock period. As many as 51 GPIOs map onto the 16 external interrupt lines.

Two 5 MSPS ADCs with 12, 10, 8 or 6-bit resolution and up to 21 external channels, some shared between ADC1 and ADC2; each channel can be single-ended or differential, converted singly or in scan sequences. Internal channels: temperature sensor on ADC1 channel 16, VBAT/2 on ADC1 channel 17, VREFINT on channel 18 of both ADCs, and the OPAMP2 reference on ADC2 channel 17. Dual modes give simultaneous or interleaved sampling and single-shunt current reading. Each ADC has three analog watchdogs that interrupt when a conversion leaves a programmed window, and DMA support. TIM1, TIM2, TIM3, TIM6 and TIM15 events can start regular and injected conversions.

An on-chip sensor gives a voltage VSENSE that rises linearly with temperature, read on ADC1_IN16. Its offset varies from part to part, so uncalibrated it suits only measuring changes; each part carries factory calibration readings in read-only system memory.
VREFINT is a bandgap reference for the ADCs and comparators, read on ADC1_IN18 and ADC2_IN18. Its value is measured on every part in production and stored read-only in system memory.
VBAT can exceed VDDA, so it reaches ADC1_IN17 through an internal divide-by-2 bridge: the conversion reads half the battery voltage.

Three 12-bit DAC channels: DAC1_OUT1 buffered, DAC1_OUT2 and DAC2_OUT1 unbuffered, each a resistor string feeding an inverting amplifier. Output is monotonic at 8 or 12 bits; 12-bit data may be aligned left or right; channels can update in step or convert together or apart; DAC1 alone generates noise and triangle waves; every channel has DMA and external conversion triggers.

OPAMP2 can be wired as a follower (internally or externally), as a programmable-gain amplifier with gain 2, 4, 8 or 16, or as an amplifier or filter with external parts. It has an 8 MHz gain-bandwidth product, rail-to-rail input and output and 0.5 mA output drive. Its output is measured through an external ADC channel.

Three fast rail-to-rail comparators (COMP2, COMP4, COMP6) with selectable output polarity. The inverting reference is an I/O, a DAC output, or VREFINT or 1/4, 1/2 or 3/4 of it. Each can wake the part from Stop and drive interrupts and timer breaks.

TIM1 is a 6-channel three-phase PWM timer with complementary outputs and programmable dead time; its counter can freeze and its outputs shut off in debug. TIM2 (32-bit) and TIM3 (16-bit) are full general-purpose timers with four channels and quadrature encoder input. TIM15 has two channels with one complementary output; TIM16 and TIM17 one channel each with a complementary output. TIM6 and TIM7 are basic 16-bit timers, mainly to trigger the DAC. Timers link to one another for synchronization and chaining, and each has its own DMA requests.

The independent watchdog is a 12-bit down-counter with an 8-bit prescaler clocked from the 40 kHz LSI, so it runs in Stop and Standby; it is started by hardware or software through option bytes and can serve as a free-running timer. The window watchdog is a 7-bit down-counter on the main clock with an early-warning interrupt. Both can freeze in debug. SysTick is a 24-bit auto-reload down-counter with its own interrupt and selectable clock, intended for an RTOS.

The RTC and five 32-bit backup registers (20 bytes) run from VDD or, without it, from VBAT. The backup registers survive system and power resets and Standby wake-up. The RTC is a BCD calendar with sub-seconds, 12 or 24-hour time, automatic month-length and leap-year handling, two alarms that wake from Stop and Standby, a 50 Hz or 60 Hz reference input to improve accuracy, on-the-fly correction of 1 to 32767 clock pulses, digital calibration in 1 ppm steps, two tamper pins with filters, a timestamp input, and a 17-bit periodic wake-up counter. It is clocked from a 32.768 kHz crystal, a resonator or oscillator, the 40 kHz LSI, or HSE/32.

One I2C, master or slave, at 100 kHz, 400 kHz or 1 MHz (Fast-mode Plus), 7 and 10-bit addresses with two slave addresses (one maskable), analog and programmable digital noise filters, SMBus 2.0 and PMBus 1.1 support (ARP, host notify, PEC, timeouts, ALERT) and DMA. Its clock domain is independent of the CPU, so I2C1 can wake the part from Stop on an address match (not with the digital filter on).
Three USARTs to 9 Mbit/s, all with DMA. USART1 adds hardware CTS/RTS, IrDA SIR, LIN master/slave, smartcard, Modbus, auto baud detection, receiver timeout and wake-up from Stop.
One SPI, master or slave, to 18 Mbit/s full-duplex or simplex, frames of 4 to 16 bits, 8 master baud rates from a 3-bit prescaler, hardware CRC, Rx/Tx FIFOs, NSS pulse mode and TI mode.
CAN 2.0A and 2.0B active to 1 Mbit/s, 11-bit and 29-bit identifiers, three transmit mailboxes, two 3-stage receive FIFOs and 14 scalable filter banks.

TIM16 and TIM17 combine internally into an IR remote-control output on PB9 or PA13: TIM17 channel 1 makes the carrier and TIM16 channel 1 the envelope, the two output-compare signals ANDed onto IR_OUT.

The touch sensing controller measures capacitive keys, sliders and wheels by charge transfer from the electrode onto a sampling capacitor until it reaches a threshold, in hardware. Up to 18 channels in six groups of four I/Os, one I/O of each group holding the sampling capacitor. PA4, PA5 and PA6 have reduced touch sensitivity and are suggested as sampling-capacitor I/Os.
Arm SWJ-DP: JTAG or serial-wire debug, with JTMS and JTCK shared with SWDIO and SWCLK; a sequence on TMS switches between JTAG-DP and SW-DP.

Voltages are referred to VSS. Minimum and maximum figures hold over the worst case of temperature, supply and frequency, tested on every part at 25 °C and at the top of the selected ambient range; figures marked as characterization or design are sample statistics (mean ± 3σ) and not production-tested. Typical figures are at 25 °C with VDD = VDDA = 3.3 V and are not tested. Typical ADC accuracy figures cover 95 % of a sample lot over temperature (mean ± 2σ). Pin parameters are measured with a 50 pF load from the pin to ground.

Every supply pair (VDD/VSS, VDDA/VSSA) gets ceramic filter capacitors placed as near the pins as possible, or under them on the far side of the board: one 100 nF per VDD pin (four on the LQFP64) plus one 4.7 µF on the VDD rail, and 10 nF plus 1 µF on VDDA. VBAT takes a 1.65 V to 3.6 V source. VREF+ and VREF- of the ADC and DAC are VDDA and VSSA.
Supply currents are measured separately in the VBAT (IDD_VBAT), VDD (IDD) and VDDA (IDDA) lines; the part's total consumption is IDD plus IDDA.

I/O current has a static and a dynamic part. An input with its pull-up draws current whenever something outside holds it low (the pull resistor values give it); an external pull-down or load on an output adds its own. An input sitting at a level between the thresholds draws current through its Schmitt trigger; analog mode avoids that, and ADC inputs are set to analog. A floating input can settle mid-level or toggle on noise, so unused pins go to analog mode, get a pull-up or pull-down, or become outputs. Each switching output draws from VDD to charge its load and internal capacitance.

In bypass mode the HSE (or LSE) oscillator is off and OSC_IN (or OSC32_IN) is an ordinary GPIO input: an external clock must meet the I/O input characteristics as well as the user clock timing (high and low times at least tw, edges no slower than tr and tf, period T).

The HSE runs from a 4 MHz to 32 MHz crystal or ceramic resonator between OSC_IN and OSC_OUT. The resonator and its load capacitors sit as close to the pins as possible, to limit output distortion and start-up time. CL1 and CL2 are high-quality ceramic capacitors for high-frequency use, typically 5 pF to 25 pF and normally equal, chosen for the crystal: the crystal's specified load capacitance is CL1 and CL2 in series plus the pin and board capacitance, for which about 10 pF is a rough figure. A series REXT on OSC_OUT is sized for the crystal. The 200 kΩ feedback resistor is inside.

The LSE runs from a 32.768 kHz crystal or ceramic resonator between OSC32_IN and OSC32_OUT, with a load capacitor from each end to ground, all placed close to the pins. No resistor goes between OSC32_IN and OSC32_OUT: one is not needed and must not be fitted. LSEDRV[1:0] sets the drive from lower to higher.

Susceptibility is characterized on samples running a simple program that toggles two LEDs. ESD (IEC 61000-4-2) is applied to every pin, and fast transient bursts (IEC 61000-4-4) to VDD and VSS through 100 pF, until the LEDs show a functional disturbance; a reset restores normal operation. EMC results depend strongly on the application software: it should handle a corrupted program counter, unexpected resets and corrupted critical data, and can be pre-qualified by holding NRST or the oscillator pins low for 1 s and by applying ESD within the rated range. Emission is measured to IEC 61967-2 with the same two-LED program.

Driving an I/O below VSS or above VDD injects current and is to be avoided in normal operation; the susceptibility figures show how much a pin withstands before the part misbehaves. Analog pins that may be pulled negative benefit from a Schottky diode to ground.

Every I/O meets both CMOS and TTL input levels without configuration. Over VDD 2.0 V to 3.6 V the production-tested limits are VIL max 0.3 VDD and VIH min 0.7 VDD; the design-simulated thresholds are VIL max 0.3 VDD + 0.07 and VIH min 0.445 VDD + 0.398 for TC and TTa pins, and VIL max 0.475 VDD - 0.2 and VIH min 0.5 VDD + 0.2 for FT and FTf pins. TTL levels are VIL max 0.8 V and VIH min 2 V. Between the two thresholds the input state is not defined.

A GPIO sinks or sources up to ±8 mA at the specified VOL/VOH and up to ±20 mA with relaxed levels. The current sourced by all I/Os plus the MCU's maximum run current from VDD stays within ΣIVDD, and the current sunk plus the run current into VSS within ΣIVSS (current characteristics).

NRST has a CMOS Schmitt input with a permanent 40 kΩ (typ) pull-up to VDD and a pulse filter: pulses under 100 ns are ignored and pulses over 500 ns are seen. A 0.1 µF capacitor from NRST to ground, as close to the chip as possible, guards against stray resets; a push button to ground gives a manual reset. Whatever drives NRST must take it below VIL(NRST) max or the reset is missed.

The I2C meets the I2C-bus specification (rev. 03) timing for Standard-mode (100 kbit/s), Fast-mode (400 kbit/s) and Fast-mode Plus (1 Mbit/s) when configured as the reference manual describes. SDA and SCL are not true open-drain: in open-drain mode the PMOS to VDD is switched off but still present. Only FTf pins meet the Fm+ low-level output current. Every SDA and SCL I/O has an analog spike filter.

In slave mode NSS falls tsu(NSS) before the first SCK edge and rises th(NSS) after the last; MISO is driven ta(SO) after NSS falls, is valid tv(SO) after each shifting edge, holds th(SO) and floats tdis(SO) after NSS rises; MOSI is sampled with tsu(SI) and th(SI) round the sampling edge, whose position follows CPHA and CPOL. In master mode MOSI is valid tv(MO) after the shifting edge and MISO needs tsu(MI) and th(MI). CAN_TX and CAN_RX follow the I/O port characteristics.

ET, the total unadjusted error, is the largest deviation of the real transfer curve from the ideal one. EO, offset error, is the deviation of the first real transition from the first ideal one; EG, gain error, that of the last real transition from the last ideal one. ED, differential linearity error, is the largest deviation of a real step from the ideal 1 LSB step; EL, integral linearity error, the largest deviation of any real transition from the line joining the end points. 1 LSB (ideal) is VDDA/4096 at 12 bits.

A source VAIN with resistance RAIN drives the input pin AINx. The pin has a diode (VT about 0.6 V) to VDD and one to ground and leaks up to ±1 µA; inside, the sample-and-hold charges CADC through RADC. RAIN must stay under the maximum for the chosen sampling time and resolution. Cparasitic, the board plus pad capacitance (about 7 pF for the pad), loads the pin; a large Cparasitic degrades accuracy, which a lower fADC recovers. Supply decoupling follows the power-supply scheme, with the 10 nF a good-quality ceramic as close to the chip as possible.
Each DAC channel has an output buffer that lowers the output impedance so DAC_OUTx can drive a load (RL to ground, CL) without an external op-amp; the BOFFx bit in DAC_CR bypasses the buffer.

The top of the LQFP32 carries the product identification on two lines (STM32F and 303K8T6), a Y WW field, a revision code R and a pin 1 mark at the lower left. Parts marked ES or E, or shipped with an engineering-sample notice, are not qualified for production.

Each temperature suffix guarantees an ambient range at full dissipation and a maximum junction temperature, so working out the real dissipation shows which suffix an application needs. Worked case: TAmax = 82 °C, IDDmax = 50 mA at VDD = 3.5 V, 20 outputs low at 8 mA and 0.4 V and 8 outputs low at 20 mA and 1.3 V: PINTmax = 175 mW, PIOmax = 272 mW, PDmax = 447 mW. With 55 °C/W for the LQFP48 the example reaches TJmax = 82 °C + (55 °C/W × 236.6 mW) = 95.01 °C, inside the suffix 6 junction range (–40 °C to 105 °C), so suffix 6 is the minimum.

STM32F303K8T6 reads: STM32 family, F general-purpose, 303 subfamily, K 32 pins, 8 for 64 KB of flash, T LQFP package, 6 for -40 °C to 85 °C. A 7 in the temperature place is -40 °C to 105 °C; a TR option is tape and reel.
